title: Worksheet — Units, Dimensions and Vectors (Class 12 NIOS Physics)
instructions: Attempt all 10 questions in your notebook. Show every step of your working for the subjective questions; choose the single best option for MCQs. Answers without working will not receive full marks. Total time: 50 minutes.

questions.question: The SI unit of pressure is the:
questions.explanation: Pa = N/m² is the SI unit of pressure.

questions.question: Force is a fundamental SI quantity.
questions.explanation: Force is derived (F = ma); the seven fundamentals are length, mass, time, current, temperature, amount, luminous intensity.

questions.question: The dimensional formula of force is [M L T^____].
Which of the following has the SAME dimensional formula as work?
questions.explanation: Work = F·d → [M L² T⁻²]; torque = r × F → [M L² T⁻²]. Same dimensions despite different physical meanings.

questions.question: The magnitude of the resultant of two perpendicular forces 8 N and 6 N is:
Check whether the equation v² = u² + 2 a s is dimensionally consistent (v, u: velocities; a: acceleration; s: displacement). Show your working.
questions.answer: [v²] = (LT⁻¹)² = L²T⁻². [u²] = L²T⁻². [2 a s] = (LT⁻²)·L = L²T⁻². All three terms have the same dimensions L²T⁻², so the equation is dimensionally consistent.
questions.explanation: Apply the principle of homogeneity term by term.

questions.question: Five measurements of a length give 12.4, 12.5, 12.3, 12.5, 12.4 cm. Compute the mean, the mean absolute error, and the percentage error.
questions.explanation: Mean → deviations → mean absolute error → divide by mean for relative, multiply by 100 for percentage.

questions.question: If \vec{a} = 3î + 4ĵ and \vec{b} = î − 2ĵ, find (i) \vec{a} + \vec{b}, (ii) \vec{a} · \vec{b}, and (iii) the magnitude |\vec{a} − \vec{b}|.
questions.explanation: Add / subtract / dot are component-wise; magnitude uses Pythagoras.

questions.question: (a) Resolve a force of 50 N acting at 53° above the +x axis into x- and y-components. Take cos 53° ≈ 0.6 and sin 53° ≈ 0.8. (b) Then find the work done on a body that moves under this force through a displacement \vec{d} = (4 m)î.
questions.answer: (a) F_x = F cos θ = 50 × 0.6 = 30 N. F_y = F sin θ = 50 × 0.8 = 40 N. So \vec{F} = 30î + 40ĵ N. (b) W = \vec{F} · \vec{d} = (30)(4) + (40)(0) = 120 J. So 120 J of work is done.
questions.explanation: Components first, then dot product with the displacement vector.

questions.question: (a) State the principle of dimensional homogeneity. (b) Use dimensional analysis to derive the dependence of the period T of a simple pendulum on its length L and gravitational acceleration g (up to a dimensionless constant). (c) State two limitations of dimensional analysis.
questions.answer: (a) Principle of dimensional homogeneity: in any physically valid equation every term must have the same dimensions. (b) Assume T = k L^a g^b. Match dimensions: T¹ = L^a (LT⁻²)^b = L^(a+b) T^(−2b). T-equation: −2b = 1 → b = −1/2. L-equation: a + b = 0 → a = 1/2. Hence T ∝ √(L/g). The actual constant is 2π (not fixable by dimensions alone). (c) Limitations: (i) dimensional analysis cannot determine dimensionless constants like 2π or 1/2, (ii) it cannot detect missing terms with the same dimensions as the kept terms, (iii) it cannot determine functional forms like sin(x) or exp(x).
questions.explanation: Standard pendulum-period dimensional argument; finishes with the limitations the chapter emphasises.
